description: We are a group of students from ITLP, four computer system engineers, one biochemistry engineer and an artificial intelligence engineer. We are all seeking to learn from this experience.
summary: The project Earthmonizer consists of a webapp in which the users can audibly experience maps of Earth. It is presented through a jukebox-like interface where users can select specific layers to visualize and listen to by pressing the buttons on the jukebox. It offers an alternative to the conventional visual representation of information in maps. With this, the information's influence extends to the sense of hearing as well, creating a larger impact. An alternative meant to clearly translate optical data to users with limited eyesight and those who simply wish to interact with it in a more engaging form.
details:
Spacecats' project solution  


--> "See it, hear it, feel it!".

The jukebox-inspired interface is designed to provide users with an intuitive and engaging navigation experience. Its digital buttons allow users to select different layers of information, which can then be explored through sound. To navigate through the map, users can either adjust the progress bar or directly drag the Earth map using the mouse, allowing them to move forward or backward through the data. Both the visual and auditory representations respond simultaneously to user interaction. As the map moves, a prominent highlighted line with contrasting thickness and color, accompanied by dots, indicates the most significant locations within the selected map layer. 

Additionally, the web application incorporates screen-reading functionality to facilitate navigation and improve accessibility for users with visual impairments. 
  

Earthmonizer was built using original ideas, names and user interface design. As for the tools employed, these include Python, Github, HTML, CCS, Javascript and a bit of AI.

Parts made using AI:  

Sonification: We used AI as a helping guide to understand certain functions in Python and which libraries to use.  

User interface: AI was employed in the design of the functional elements and adapting them to our own original designs made by hand.  

Logistics: AI was used to understand some concepts from Python.
